context_label: Recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer after platinum
title: Cemiplimab for cervical cancer after platinum chemotherapy
schedule_label: One infusion every three weeks (21 days), while it is helping and side effects remain manageable.
schedule_summary: One infusion every three weeks (21 days), while it is helping and side effects remain manageable.
purpose: Cemiplimab helps the immune system recognise cancer that has grown during or after platinum chemotherapy. The aim is to slow cancer growth and help you live longer.
indication_text: Adults with recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer that progressed on or after platinum chemotherapy, ECOG 0–2 and adequate organ function. NCCP 00812a specifies no PD-L1 threshold. Review prior checkpoint inhibitor exposure under current Irish sequencing guidance.
administration_text: Cemiplimab (Libtayo) 350 mg is given into a vein over about 30 minutes.
monitoring_summary: Blood count, kidney and liver tests, blood glucose and a review of changes in breathing, bowels, skin and energy.
review_status: Feasibility build. Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Cemiplimab
agents.explanation: Helps immune cells recognise and attack cancer by blocking the PD-1 signal. This can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.

common_effects.title: What you may notice
common_effects.text: Tiredness, itchy skin or changes in bowel habit may occur. A persistent or worsening symptom needs review, even if it seems mild.

serious_effects.title: Lung inflammation · Cemiplimab
serious_effects.text: Phone urgently for new breathlessness or a persistent cough.

serious_effects.title: Bowel inflammation · Cemiplimab
serious_effects.text: Phone about new diarrhoea, cramps or blood in stools the day they occur.

serious_effects.title: Liver inflammation · Cemiplimab
serious_effects.text: Report yellow skin, dark urine or pain under the right ribs.

serious_effects.title: Kidney inflammation · Cemiplimab
serious_effects.text: Tell the team promptly about reduced urine or new swelling.

serious_effects.title: Hormone gland changes · Cemiplimab
serious_effects.text: Phone about unusual weakness, headache, dizziness, marked thirst or passing much more urine.

serious_effects.title: Skin inflammation · Cemiplimab
serious_effects.text: Report a spreading rash. Painful rash, blistering or peeling needs urgent help.

serious_effects.title: Heart, muscles or nerves
serious_effects.text: New chest pain, palpitations with weakness, difficulty swallowing or trouble lifting the eyelids need urgent assessment. Severe chest pain, collapse or severe breathing difficulty needs 112 or 999.

questions.q: Do I need a positive PD-L1 tumour test for this treatment?
questions.a: The Irish cemiplimab indication after platinum does not require a minimum PD-L1 score. Your team checks your previous treatments and whether immunotherapy is suitable.

questions.q: How will the team decide what happens next?
questions.a: Your specialist compares scans and symptoms over time. If you need a treatment pause for immune inflammation, you may need tests, steroids or hormone replacement.

questions.q: I already had pembrolizumab. Can I change to cemiplimab?
questions.a: Tell your team why pembrolizumab stopped. If cancer grew on it for the same advanced disease, switching to cemiplimab is generally outside the Irish pathway. Intolerance can be assessed separately.

questions.q: Could a new symptom still be from immunotherapy after my last infusion?
questions.a: Yes. Immune inflammation can start later. Keep your alert card and tell any doctor or nurse the medicine name and date of your last dose.

support.title: Cemiplimab
support.text: Carry your immunotherapy alert card and contact oncology for new symptoms, even after treatment has stopped.

support.title: Immune alert card
support.text: Keep the hospital’s immunotherapy alert card with you. Show it at emergency visits, during admissions and after treatment has ended.

support.title: Early contact
support.text: Some new symptoms need blood or stool tests, scans or steroids. Contact oncology before starting leftover steroids or treating diarrhoea yourself.

support.title: Nausea support
support.text: There is usually no preventive anti-sickness treatment for this infusion alone. Contact your team about persistent vomiting.

teachback: Can you show your immunotherapy alert card, name your next infusion date and say which new symptoms to phone about?
consent_support: Discuss the intended benefit, other treatment options, immune inflammation, possible steroid treatment and the possibility of long-term hormone replacement.
safety_note: Call the 24-hour oncology team immediately about new breathlessness, persistent cough, new diarrhoea, blood in stools, severe weakness, yellow eyes or a severe headache. Symptoms can start after treatment ends. Carry your immunotherapy alert card.
urgent_extra: Call the 24-hour oncology team immediately about new breathlessness, persistent cough, new diarrhoea, blood in stools, severe weakness, yellow eyes or a severe headache. Symptoms can start after treatment ends. Carry your immunotherapy alert card.

evidence.title: EMPOWER-Cervical 1 · final overall survival
evidence.interpretation: In a study of 608 people, those assigned cemiplimab lived longer as a group than those assigned another chemotherapy medicine. The figures describe groups and cannot predict one person’s outcome.
evidence.limitations: Evidence applies to the post-platinum trial population. Benefit after progression on a prior PD-1 inhibitor is unestablished in this comparison.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests, blood glucose and thyroid function. Hepatitis B and C screening is also required.
List any steroids or hormone replacements and tell the team about autoimmune illness, diabetes or previous immunotherapy reactions.

rows.label: Before each infusion
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests, blood glucose and a review of changes in breathing, bowels, skin and energy.
Bring your alert card and medicines list. Ring between visits about new symptoms, even if your last blood tests were normal.

rows.label: Every 3–6 weeks
cells: Thyroid blood tests check for immune inflammation. Other hormone tests depend on your symptoms.
Ask for your blood test dates and the date for your next scan.

monitoring_schedule.note: Your team books scans and any extra blood tests according to your symptoms and treatment plan.
